name: Immunodeficiency due to MASP-2 deficiency

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic variants in the MASP2 gene by molecular genetic testing
Demonstrated deficiency or functional impairment of the lectin complement pathway activity
History of recurrent bacterial infections, particularly respiratory tract infections
Exclusion of other primary immunodeficiencies and secondary causes of immunodeficiency

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of pathogenic MASP2 gene variants plus documented lectin pathway deficiency and clinical history of recurrent infections
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Functional assays of lectin pathway activity are critical to confirm diagnosis alongside genetic testing.

pathognomonic.notes: Often severe and persistent infections including pneumonia and bronchitis

common.symptomName: Recurrent skin and soft tissue infections
searchTerms: repeated skin and soft tissue infections
frequent infections of skin and tissues

common.notes: Frequent middle ear infections in childhood
Persistent inflammation of the paranasal sinuses

common.symptomName: Failure to thrive in pediatric patients
common.notes: Due to recurrent infections and chronic illness
searchTerms: failure to gain weight and grow

occasional.notes: Enlarged lymph nodes due to chronic immune stimulation

rare.notes: Bacterial meningitis secondary to complement deficiency
Inflammatory joint involvement in some cases

laboratory: Reduced lectin pathway complement activity (e.g., low MASP-2 serum levels)
Normal classical and alternative complement pathway activity
Normal or mildly decreased immunoglobulin levels
imaging: Chest radiographs showing recurrent pneumonia or bronchiectasis
Sinus CT scans demonstrating chronic sinusitis
other: Functional assays confirming lectin pathway impairment
Exclusion of other immunodeficiencies by immunophenotyping

distinguishingFeatures: MBL deficiency affects upstream lectin pathway but MASP-2 deficiency specifically impairs protease activity
MBL deficiency may have milder clinical phenotype
CVID presents with hypogammaglobulinemia and broader antibody deficiency
MASP-2 deficiency primarily affects complement lectin pathway

redFlags: Severe recurrent bacterial pneumonia in early childhood
Recurrent invasive infections despite normal immunoglobulin levels
Family history of complement pathway deficiencies or unexplained immunodeficiency
references: Degn SE, Jensenius JC. The lectin pathway of complement and its role in innate immunity. Immunobiology. 2011.
Thiel S, et al. MASP-2 deficiency and its clinical implications. Orphanet J Rare Dis. 2015.
Orphanet: Immunodeficiency due to MASP-2 deficiency (ORPHA:331187)
